record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Special cases of the click-cloud problem
record.original_question: In the same lattice-click setting, analyze the special cases in which the translating set is a line segment, a polygon, or a circle.

evidence.quote: Question 3: Analyze special cases of the segment; a polygon; a circle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following "click–cloud" setting in the Euclidean plane. Fix the integer lattice $\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and a compact set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, called the translating set. For each translation vector $v\in\mathbb{R}^2$, the translate $S+v$ "clicks" the lattice points contained in it, i.e. produces the (finite) configuration
$$C_S(v)\;=\;(S+v)\cap\Lambda\;\subset\;\Lambda.$$
The "click–cloud" of $S$ is the collection of all such configurations,
$$\mathcal{C}(S)\;=\;\{\,C_S(v)\,:\,v\in\mathbb{R}^2\,\},$$
considered as a family of finite subsets of $\Lambda$ (equivalently, of finite point patterns up to integer translation). One is interested in the combinatorial and geometric structure of $\mathcal{C}(S)$: which finite subsets of $\Lambda$ occur as clicks, how their cardinalities are distributed, and how $\mathcal{C}(S)$ depends on the size, shape, and orientation of $S$.

Problem. Carry out a complete analysis of the click–cloud $\mathcal{C}(S)$ in each of the following three special cases, describing all configurations that occur, the dependence on size and orientation of $S$, and the transitions between different configuration types:

(a) $S$ is a line segment of length $\ell>0$ with direction $\theta\in[0,\pi)$;

(b) $S$ is a convex (or general) polygon, parametrised by its vertex set;

(c) $S$ is a closed disk (circle) of radius $r>0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a 2021/2022 collection of open problems from the CIRM workshop on Differential Geometry, Billiards, and Geometric Optics, published in Arnold Mathematical Journal. No subsequent publication resolving the three special cases (segment, polygon, circle) of the click-cloud problem could be located.
